findings.title: At 200% zoom the header collapses: kind line one letter per line, header taller than the panel
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured, dial-configured, dial-groups; first screen after opening; 160x410 and 189x410 (320 and 378 panels at 200%)
findings.observed: MEASURED at 160 px: the key header is 476 px tall on a 410 px panel. The kind line 'Sensor Reading key' renders 16 lines at 0 px width, one letter per line. The theme gallery starts at y=503, off the first screen. At 189 px: header 232 px, kind line broken mid-word ('Sens / or / Readi / ng / key', 5 lines at 29 px), gallery at y=260. Dial at 160 px: header 285 px, kind line 5 lines at 17 px. Cause (READ): the header is a non-wrapping row of the face (72 px; the dial face is at least 112 px) plus a text column, and the fold pair takes about 52 px of that column.
findings.evidence: zoom.mjs, verify.mjs, headwrap.mjs; screenshots %TEMP%\hw-r3-a11y\zoom\key-configured-160.png and key-configured-189.png; verify.txt rows '160 key-configured base head 476 kind 16 line(s) @0px galleryTop 503'. axe and the lab's own checks reported 0 issues in these same states.
findings.correction: pi.css: @media (max-width: 239px) { .hw-head { flex-wrap: wrap; } }. The text column already has a flex-basis of 160 px (key) or 140 px (dial), so it drops below the face only when it would be narrower than that.
findings.tradeoff: Below 240 px the face sits above the text instead of beside it. At 210-239 px the key header grows a little (230 px: 150 to 186 px, already unpinned). An unconditional flex-wrap is NOT safe: measured, it unpins the dial header at 252-270 px and the key header at 252 px.
findings.acceptance_test: At 160x410 and 189x410, for key-configured and dial-configured: .hw-head-kind is at most 2 lines and #theme-gallery top < 410. Verified by injection: 160 px key 476 to 202 px, gallery 503 to 229; 189 px 232 to 186 px. At 240, 252, 270, 290, 320 and 373 px, header height and position:sticky equal the baseline (verified identical).

findings.title: Replace shared settings: 5 s confirm window re-arms instead of applying
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured, all open, valid JSON in the shared well, keyboard Enter on 'Replace shared settings', 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: the first Enter arms the button. Its label becomes 'Click again to replace for all keys and dials' and the polite note says 'This replaces the shared settings every HWiNFO key and dial uses. Click again to confirm.' A second Enter at 5.3 s re-armed instead of applying: setGlobalSettings count stayed 0 and the same note repeated. The note is 15 words, about 5 s of speech at 180 wpm, so a screen reader user who waits for it to finish misses the window. READ: armedUntil = Date.now() + 5000 (line 4248).
findings.evidence: behaviors.mjs step 3 output: 'second Enter at 5.3 s ... globalWrites 0'. The limit is set by the content and cannot be turned off, adjusted or extended, and no WCAG 2.2.1 exception applies.
findings.affected_user: screen reader, switch/motor, anyone slower than 5 s
findings.correction: Keep the armed state until the button loses focus or the well is edited (no timer), or use at least 20 s. Word it 'Press again to confirm'.
findings.tradeoff: A stale armed button could apply on a much later accidental press. Disarm on blur and on input.
findings.acceptance_test: Arm, wait 10 s with focus on the button, press Enter: exactly one setGlobalSettings. Arm, Tab away and back, press Enter: it only re-arms.

findings.title: Copy support report drops focus to the page and never announces its result
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured, all open, keyboard Enter on 'Copy support report', plugin reply delayed 600 ms (sim replyDelayMs), clipboard stubbed, 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: document.activeElement is BODY during the wait and still BODY after the reply, because the button sets disabled=true while waiting. The outcome ('Copied to clipboard', 'Plugin not responding' or 'Copy failed') exists only as the button's text for 2 s and is in no live region. Chrome kept the sequential-focus starting point (the next Tab reached the following summary), but assistive technology loses its place.
findings.evidence: behaviors.mjs step 4: 'during wait focus = BODY ... disabled true'; 'after reply focus = BODY label "Copied to clipboard"'; no live region contains it. WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).
findings.correction: Use aria-disabled="true" plus the existing 'waiting' guard instead of disabled. Speak the outcome through the shell's polite announcer (hw.announce) or a role=status next to the button.
findings.tradeoff: The button stays focusable while waiting. The guard must stop a second press from sending a duplicate request.
findings.acceptance_test: Enter with a 600 ms reply delay: focus stays on the button throughout, and a polite region's text becomes the outcome exactly once.

findings.title: Missing rotation or detail member is marked only by color, a dashed edge and a hover title; its name is a raw key
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-configured with rotationKeys [gpu, 'f0099999:0:1000000', hot] and a fine primary reading (so no status block); key-details with the same key in detailKeys; 373x410; also in forced colors
findings.observed: MEASURED: the chip reads 'f0099999:0:1000000' in amber (#ffcf70) with a dashed border. Nothing visible says 'not found', and the set note still says 'Rotation moves through these 3 readings only'. Screen readers get more than sighted users: the option's AX name is 'f0099999:0:1000000 (not in HWiNFO's current list)' from an sr-only span, and the detail button carries the title as its description. Sighted users get only a title tooltip, which never appears for keyboard focus (the option is an activedescendant item and the list holds focus). In forced colors only a 1 px dashed border remains. INFERRED: the raw key is the name because rotation settings store keys, not labels.
findings.evidence: ax.mjs output; screenshot pair-rotation-missing-member.png (normal vs forced). READ: title at lines 430 and 1781; sr-only note at 441-446.
findings.affected_user: everyone sighted (beginners most), keyboard, forced colors
findings.correction: Make the existing sr-only note a visible short pill ('not found'), in the same pill style as 'on dial' with flex:none, on both rotation and detail chips, and remove the sr-only duplicate. Optionally the set note counts it ('3 readings, 1 not in HWiNFO's list').
findings.tradeoff: Chips get wider. A chip that is both on the dial and missing shows two pills. The e2e option-name assertions change.
findings.acceptance_test: In that fixture the missing chip shows visible 'not found' text at 373 and 160 px and in forced colors, and its AX name contains the phrase exactly once.

findings.title: Fold pair: bottom quarter of both buttons is dead in the dial header when the reading name runs under them
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups (reading 'GPU Hot Spot Temperature' in a 161 px text column), default folds and all-open, pointer on Open all / Fold all, 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED with elementFromPoint over every CSS pixel: only 75.4% of Open all and 81.0% of Fold all answer the button. Rows 21-27 of 28 go to p#head-reading, whose first text line wraps under the pair. Effective height is about 21 px, there is no hover feedback in that strip, and a click there does nothing. Key-configured, dial-configured and control reach 99%. Cause: the -6px bottom margin hangs the pair into the next line, and the later paragraph's inline text wins hit testing.
findings.evidence: fold-hit.mjs output ('373 dial-groups Open all sections self 75.4% others {p#head-reading: 196} deadRows ...21..27'); hit.mjs 'Fold all sections box 28x28 hit 80.7%'.
findings.correction: .hw-folds { position: relative; z-index: 1; }. Verified by injection: dial-groups pair back to 99%, and nothing else changes at 373/320/189/160.
findings.tradeoff: On hover the pair's raised fill covers the top 6 px of the reading name under it. An alternative with no overlap is a -2px bottom margin, which costs 4 px of header height.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-groups at 373x410: at least 98% of the pixels in both 28x28 boxes resolve to the button.

findings.title: Keyboard focus on the checked theme chip shows as a 1 px sliver
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured and dial-groups; Tab into the gallery (the Tab stop is always the checked chip); 373x410 at DPR 1.5 (the host's)
findings.observed: MEASURED: the button's 2 px focus outline (offset 1 px) overlaps the face's 2 px checked ring (offset 1 px). About 1 CSS px of blue shows outside the white ring, and the two colors differ by only 1.59:1. The arrow keys check whatever they focus and the theme line does not change, so entering the gallery barely changes the screen. Every other Tab stop measured shows a full 2 px ring.
findings.evidence: focus.mjs; crop %TEMP%\hw-r3-a11y\chip-focus-pair.png (before/after); contrast.txt 'FOCUS ring vs checked-chip ring 1.59:1'. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) is met because a change exists; 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) is not met.
findings.correction: .hw-look .hw-theme:focus-visible { outline-offset: 3px; }. This gives a separate 2 px blue ring with a 1 px gap outside the checked ring (verified: verify\chip-focus-fix.png).
findings.tradeoff: The ring extends 5 px outside the chip into the current 6 px grid gap and toward the theme name line. A gap under 5 px would let it touch a neighbor.
findings.acceptance_test: Tab into the gallery at DPR 1.5: at least 2 CSS px of focus color, separated from the checked ring, on all four sides.

findings.title: Custom detail list costs 83 Tab presses for 12 readings (the rotation editor costs 3)
findings.area: Sensor Reading > Press > custom detail list (tile editor)
findings.state_task_viewport: key-details with 12 custom readings (tabcost.mjs); stock key-details fixture; keyboard; 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: 83 Tab presses from 'Add readings' to 'Readings per tile' for 12 readings. The same 12 readings in the dial rotation editor take 3 presses (search to title). The stock key-details fixture spends 31 stops on 5 readings (traverse stops 24-54), because every cell exposes rename, up, down and remove and every tile its grip, size and add, each as a separate Tab stop.
findings.affected_user: keyboard, switch access, power users building long lists
findings.correction: One Tab stop per tile, with arrow keys moving across its controls (the APG toolbar pattern the rotation toolbar and fold pair already use). A smaller alternative: cell up/down/remove at tabindex -1, reached by arrows from the cell name.
findings.tradeoff: Less discoverable for sighted keyboard users. It needs a short sr-only instruction, and e2e tab-order expectations change.
findings.acceptance_test: With 12 readings, at most about 15 Tab presses from 'Add readings' to 'Readings per tile', and every control is still operable by keyboard.

findings.title: Threshold typo is not announced to screen reader users
findings.area: Alerts / bar range number fields (pi-shell.js validateNumber:177-186; sensor-reading.html:235-241)
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured, Alerts open, type '8o' in Warn at, 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: aria-invalid becomes true and 'Not a number. Alerts ignore this field until it is one.' appears, linked by aria-describedby. The AX description includes it, but the element is not a live region, so nothing is spoken while typing. The value '8o' is saved and alerts silently ignore it. The folded Alerts summary does say 'warn value is not a number' (good).
findings.evidence: behaviors.mjs step 2 (errorLive null; AX invalid=true with description). WCAG 3.3.1 is met; 4.1.3 Status Messages is arguable for inline validation.
findings.correction: When a field's validity flips from valid to invalid, speak the message once through hw.announce.
findings.tradeoff: It would chatter while typing unless it fires only on the transition.
findings.acceptance_test: Typing '8o' gives one polite announcement. Further invalid characters give none, and clearing the field gives none.

findings.title: At 200% zoom chip editors cut names, the 'on dial' pill and the toolbar hint, and the layout overflows sideways
findings.area: Rotation editor and detail list chips (pi.css .hw-set-chip > span:1160, .hw-set-tools-slot:1380, .hw-set-tools-hint:1392), theme name line (.hw-look-current:376)
findings.state_task_viewport: dial-groups and key-details all open; dial-configured; key-inherited with shared Ultraviolet; 189x410 and 160x410
findings.observed: MEASURED at 160 px: rotation chips read 'Hot S...' and the 'on dial' pill reads 'on d...'. That pill is the non-color cue for the current reading. Detail cell names are 38 px wide ('GPU...'). The aria-hidden hint 'Select one to move, rename or remove it' is white-space:nowrap inside a flex item without min-width:0, so it forces its slot to 207 px. At 189 and 160 px the layout is 58 and 87 px wider than the viewport, and body overflow-x:hidden cuts the hint mid-sentence with no ellipsis. The theme line 'Default · Ultraviolet' is cut at 160 px (96/103 px), and it is the only visible name of the resolved theme.
findings.correction: .hw-set-chip > .hw-chip-badge { flex: none; overflow: visible; } and .hw-set-tools-slot { min-width: 0; }. Under 240 px, let .hw-set-tools-hint and .hw-look-current wrap. Verified by injection: overflow 87 to 0, pill no longer cut.
findings.tradeoff: Under 240 px the hint can take two lines, so the toolbar slot no longer keeps one constant height (its no-shift promise) at that zoom. Names truncate slightly earlier because the pill keeps its width.
findings.acceptance_test: dial-groups at 160x410: documentElement scrollWidth == clientWidth, 'on dial' is whole, the hint is fully visible, and the theme line shows the whole resolved name.

findings.title: Forced colors: every disclosure triangle becomes a bar
findings.observed: MEASURED in emulation: open sections show a horizontal bar and closed sections a vertical bar. The 'How Display works' and 'HWiNFO setup steps' markers are bars too. Cause (READ): the grouped forced rule gives .hw-sec/.hw-sub > summary::before 'background: CanvasText', which fills the 5x10 border box of the CSS triangle. The .hw-how and .hw-inline-help markers are not covered at all.
findings.evidence: forced.mjs; pair-sections.png, pair-top.png (normal vs forced). Fixed render: pair-forced-fix.png.
findings.correction: Keep background: CanvasText for .hw-state::before only. Summary markers get border-left-color only. Add .hw-how/.hw-inline-help > summary::before { forced-color-adjust: none; border-top-color: transparent; border-bottom-color: transparent; border-left-color: LinkText; }. Verified in emulation.
findings.tradeoff: None found. Emulation only; real Windows High Contrast was not run.
findings.acceptance_test: In forced colors, closed markers point right and open markers point down, for sections, sub-sections and help disclosures.

findings.title: Forced colors: the saved reading is unmarked once the list highlight moves
findings.area: Reading combobox list (.hw-row.selected, pi.css:1054-1058; forced block)
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured, Reading combobox open, ArrowDown twice, forced-colors emulation, 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: the saved row computes to black background, white text and no outline, exactly like every other row. In normal colors it keeps a blue fill. The input still shows the saved name.
findings.evidence: forced.mjs computed styles (selectedRow outlineStyle none); pair-list.png.
findings.correction: In the forced block: .hw-row.selected, .hw-row[aria-selected="true"] { forced-color-adjust: none; background: SelectedItem; color: SelectedItemText; }. Verified in emulation (pair-forced-fix.png).
findings.tradeoff: Where SelectedItem equals Highlight, the saved row (fill) and the active row (outline) still differ by shape.
findings.acceptance_test: In forced colors, with the list open and the highlight moved, the saved row has a system-color fill and the active row an outline.

findings.title: Default chip on a Paper shared theme: link mark and dashed frame all but vanish
findings.area: Theme gallery Default chip (pi.css .hw-look .hw-theme-badge:440-446; pi-common.js FOLLOW_GLYPH comment 3419-3421)
findings.state_task_viewport: key-inherited with shared theme Paper (Default checked), 373x410, DPR 1.5
findings.observed: MEASURED: the link mark #8ecbff on the Paper face #E9E6DE is 1.39:1, and the dashed frame #b8b8b8 against the face is 1.59:1. On the six dark palettes the mark is 9.8-12.1:1 and the frame 8.6-10.6:1. READ: the code says the mark sits 'on a translucent dark badge' to stay legible on any palette, but .hw-look .hw-theme-badge sets background: none. The word 'Default' remains, so this is not a 1.4.11 failure, but the owner's 'Default keeps its link mark' cue fails for low-vision users on Paper.
findings.evidence: contrast.txt 'shared=paper: ... link mark 1.39, dashed frame vs face 1.59'; forced\gallery-shared-paper.png.
findings.correction: Draw the mark in the palette's own text color (on Paper #14120D, 15:1), or restore the dark badge only when the resolved palette is light.
findings.tradeoff: The mark is no longer always blue, or a dark square on Paper looks heavier.
findings.acceptance_test: For every shared theme, the link mark is at least 3:1 against the Default chip face.

findings.title: Text-spacing override (WCAG 1.4.12) truncates chip names
findings.area: Theme gallery chip names (.hw-look .hw-theme-value, face padding 6 px)
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured and dial panels with the standard 1.4.12 spacing override injected, 373x410 and 320x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: 'Ultraviolet' 67/70 px at 373 ('Ultraviol...'); 'Default' 41/46 px and 'Ultraviolet' 60/67 px at 320. INFERRED: the Stream Deck host probably offers no user stylesheet, so real exposure is low.
findings.affected_user: low vision / dyslexia users with spacing overrides
findings.correction: Reduce the face's horizontal padding from 6 to 4 px at these widths, or let the name shrink instead of clip.
findings.acceptance_test: Under the override at 320 and 373 px, no .hw-theme-value has scrollWidth > clientWidth.

findings.title: Reduced motion leaves three marker transitions running
findings.state_task_viewport: key-configured all open, prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulated, 373x410
findings.observed: MEASURED: the .hw-sub, .hw-how and .hw-inline-help summary markers still transition for 0.12 s. Only .hw-sec is set to 0s.
findings.correction: Extend the reduced-motion selector to .hw-sub > summary::before, .hw-how > summary::before and .hw-inline-help > summary::before.
findings.acceptance_test: Under reduce, all four markers compute transition-duration 0s.

findings.title: Default radio's description repeats its name
findings.observed: MEASURED (AX): name 'Default: follow the shared theme, currently Void', description (from title) 'Default: follows the shared theme (Void)'. Screen readers say nearly the same text twice.
findings.correction: Drop the title on the Default chip (the visible line already shows 'Default · Void'), or make it identical to the aria-label.
findings.tradeoff: The pointer tooltip goes away or duplicates the name.
findings.acceptance_test: The Default radio's AX description is empty or equal to its name.

keep_unchanged: Theme chip names on their own faces: 12.22:1 (Ember) to 21:1 (Void), 11.5 px / 600, all eight named, none clipped at 373/320/189/160 without a spacing override; each accessible name contains its visible word (label in name) (MEASURED)

Theme gallery as an APG radiogroup: one Tab stop on the checked chip; arrows check and write one field each (4 arrows = 4 single-field 'theme' writes, futureBlob kept); an unknown stored theme leaves the Tab stop on Default. Keep it: focus-without-check would break radio semantics. Arrow keys writing is selection per APG, not browsing (MEASURED)

All enabled text in 12 fixtures clears WCAG AA; the minimum is 4.51:1 (placeholder). Muted text 6.94:1 on the page and 5.73:1 on fields; focus ring #7cc4ff 7.34:1 on the page and 6.06:1 on fields; field edges 3.30:1; 'on dial' pill text 6.29:1 (MEASURED)

Focus visibility: every Tab stop measured at DPR 1.5, except A06's chip, changes more pixels than its own perimeter. No stop lacks :focus-visible, and none is hidden under the pinned header at 373/320/189/160 (MEASURED, lab + focus.mjs)
Fold toolbar: one Tab stop, arrow keys, aria-disabled buttons stay focusable, 'All sections open/folded' is announced once per press, and it writes 0 settings (plugin fold memory only) (MEASURED)

Rotation editor: a listbox per list with aria-activedescendant, one roving toolbar, an 'on dial' text pill (not color alone), and selection kept distinct from 'on dial' in both normal and forced colors (MEASURED)
Collector radios: 24x24 label hit areas, 100% hittable; arrow keys move the collector, the search label follows ('Readings for GPU'), 0 writes (MEASURED)

'Change' shared-theme action: 43x24 target, 100% of its box hittable (its negative margin overlaps the Ember chip's bottom 1 px, 41 px², harmless); it opens Advanced > Shared defaults and focuses the Theme select in view with 0 writes (MEASURED)
Recovery buttons (Retry now, HWiNFO setup steps, Reload sensor list, Pick another reading) come before the palette in Tab order (MEASURED)
Reading combobox: arrow keys browse without writing and Tab closes without committing (MEASURED here and asserted by e2e)
The folded Alerts summary names an invalid threshold ('warn value is not a number') (MEASURED)

Forced colors: chips keep their palettes and names (forced-color-adjust none), the checked chip gets a Highlight ring, focus is clearly visible (better than in normal colors), disabled buttons use GrayText, and the state dot keeps its shape cues (circle/square/diamond) (MEASURED in emulation)

Target sizes at 373 px: every control is at least 24 px effective, except native 18 px checkboxes and radios, whose wrapping labels are at least 24 px tall; the inline 'reading links' link is exempt as inline text (MEASURED)
Header status line and live regions are not re-announced per tick (READ, pi-shell renderStatus signature guard)
own_regression_risks: A01: the header wrap must stay scoped under 240 px. Measured: an unconditional flex-wrap unpins the dial header at 252-270 px and the key header at 252 px. Even when scoped, the key header at 210-239 px grows (230 px: 150 to 186 px).
A02: a timerless armed state could apply on a much later press; it must disarm on blur and on input.
A03: switching disabled to aria-disabled needs the existing 'waiting' guard, or repeated Enter sends duplicate getSupportReport requests.
A04: a visible 'not found' pill widens chips, doubles pills on a current and missing chip, and doubles speech unless the sr-only note is removed; e2e rotation option-name assertions change.
A05: z-index on the fold pair lets its hover fill cover the top 6 px of the reading name beneath it (the -2px margin alternative costs 4 px of header height).
A06: outline-offset 3px relies on the current 6 px grid gap and the 4 px gap above the chip rows; a tighter future gap would let rings touch neighbors or the theme line.
A07: roving focus inside tiles lowers discoverability for sighted keyboard users and changes e2e tab-order expectations.
A08: announcing validity on every keystroke would be noisy; announce only on the valid-to-invalid transition.
A09: letting the toolbar hint wrap under 240 px breaks the constant-height toolbar slot (the no-shift promise) at that zoom.
A11: in High Contrast themes where SelectedItem equals Highlight, the fill-versus-outline shape difference is the only distinction left.
A12: a palette-colored link mark changes its blue identity; a dark badge looks heavy on Paper.
not_run: Real screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, Narrator): every screen reader statement comes from Chrome's accessibility tree (Accessibility.getFullAXTree/getPartialAXTree), not from speech output. That includes whether aria-invalid changes or the 5 s window are announced in time.
Real Windows High Contrast / contrast themes: only Chromium's forced-colors emulation (its dark HC-like palette) was used.
The real Stream Deck host (QtWebEngine 6.9.3 / Chrome 130), its fonts and message timing, and whether it lets a person zoom the panel at all. DevTools port 23654 was untouched by rule.
Windows text scaling / system font size, and user text-spacing stylesheets in the host (1.4.12 was measured only with injected CSS).
Touch, pen, switch access and speech input (Voice Access). Label in name was checked only through AX names.
Real mouse hardware: hit areas were measured with elementFromPoint only.
e2e suites (e2e-pi-panels, e2e-pi-persistence) and anything that spawns the real plugin, by rule.
